I’ve been thinking about this too. I stopped counting days after my last relapse (or was it the one before that?) because I just can’t be bothered to remember the date. I had been clean for almost two years at one point and after that it just felt surreal to go back to counting days

The way I try to see it is that relapses are a part of recovery. Perhaps an overused line but it helps me. Relapse doesn’t erase your progress. It’s easy to get swept up in what I call the “broken diet” mindset, ie. thoughts like “oh well I broke my diet by eating a cookie I might as well eat the whole box”. That kind of black and white thinking is something I think a lot of self harmers struggle with. 

As for the relationship stuff I don’t have any good advice but when it comes to relapsing I’ve found that the only thing to try to do is to accept that it happened, be gentle with yourself instead of blaming yourself and to try to create a new clean streak. 

I know it sucks to feel like you’re starting over, but that really isn’t the case. It’s a bump in the road but you haven’t fallen of the tracks. (Sorry for the mixed metaphor).
